question: White light is composed of how many colours?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Seven**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the 1660s, English physicist and mathematician** Isaac Newton** began a series of experiments with sunlight and prisms.
 
• He demonstrated that clear **white light was composed of seven visible colors**.
 
• One of the greatest scientific **books **ever written, **Opticks**, details** Newton's findings from his experiments using prisms** to bend light.
 
• He named the **hues that comprise the visible spectrum**: **red**, **orange**, **yellow**, **green**, **blue**, **indigo**, and **violet**, or **ROYGBIV**.
 
• The small range of the electromagnetic spectrum that is visible to the human eye is known as the **visible spectrum**.
 
 
• Typically, the human eye can detect wavelengths from **380 to 700 nanometers.**
 
 
 
• Radio, gamma, and microwave radiation are additional types of **electromagnetic radiation**—energy waves that are invisible to the human eye.
 
• **Cone cells**, which are located in human eyes, are sensitive to wavelengths in the visible range. They **make it possible for us to see every hue in the rainbow.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The phenomenon of splitting light into its constituent colors is called **dispersion of light**.
 
• The bending of light as it moves from one transparent substance into another is known as **refraction**.
